commandOrSteps: Inspect the authenticated GitHub repository branch-protection and ruleset pages; query repository owner/default branch and CODEOWNERS errors through the public GitHub REST API; search workflow and scripts for DCO enforcement; compare action and runner lifecycle with current official GitHub sources.

environment.codeownersApi: Public GitHub REST API, ref codex/b07-01-ubuntu-validation

classicBranchProtection.observedText: Classic branch protections have not been configured

requiredChecksAndReviews.reason: No repository branch-protection rule or ruleset exists; repository owner is a user account, so there is no organization-parent ruleset to inherit. CI runs are informational and are not a merge gate.

dco.note: The B07 commits are manually signed off, but no required branch rule or DCO gate exists.

actionAndRunnerLifecycle.decision: Upgrade checkout and setup-node to current Node 24-compatible major releases. Pin CI to ubuntu-24.04, which has the existing project validation baseline, until Ubuntu 26.04 is tested explicitly.

expected: Determine whether remote branch controls enforce CI, review, CODEOWNERS and DCO, and verify the actual Node and Ubuntu lifecycle before changing workflow action/runtime selections.
actual: The authenticated repository settings show no classic branch protection and no repository rulesets. The public repository API confirms the owner is a user account and reports 28 Unknown owner errors across every CODEOWNERS line that references @vittrade/* teams. The checked B07 commits contain sign-off trailers, but no DCO enforcement is configured in repository workflow or remote required checks. Official GitHub notices say Node 20 was removed from Actions on 2026-09-23 and ubuntu-latest migration to Ubuntu 26.04 rolls out from 2026-10-19 through 2026-11-19. The workflow therefore needs Node 24-compatible action majors and an explicit Ubuntu 24.04 pin pending a separate Ubuntu 26.04 test.
notes: Verification records existing remote state; it does not enable protections or infer that a passing Actions run blocks a merge. CODEOWNERS ownership needs the user to supply valid GitHub user/team identities before it can be repaired.
